ask.hook_test_note: muse plugins hook test reports hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision ask as status=completed with permission_decision null; only the live runtime shows the human prompt
ask.conclusion: Ask surface exists: PreToolUse {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":…}} (exit 0) forces a human approval prompt (presentation_phase human_pending, choices allow once / abort, Notification permission_prompt) that bypasses the LLM approval judge under --approval-mode on-request (the default); a headless muse exec has no responder and waits until killed. Under untrusted it folds into the mode's own approval, which the LLM judge decided (approved, the same records as the no-hook baseline); under never it is ignored and the tool runs. PermissionRequest has no ask: hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior accepts only allow and deny. Every other ask shape (legacy {decision}, top-level permissionDecision, decision approve) is a failed hook and the tool runs (fail-open). Deny works on both events: PreToolUse permissionDecision deny → 'tool blocked by hook: <reason>'; PermissionRequest decision.behavior deny → 'tool denied by hook: <reason>'. A bare PreToolUse permissionDecision allow is rejected ('requires updatedInput').

updated_input.conclusion: Input rewrite is supported on PreToolUse through hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput, alone or with permissionDecision allow (exit 0). It replaces the whole tool_input: keys the hook omits are dropped (the model's description vanished from the bash result), and the tool runs the rewritten input (echo rewritten-540-r2 / -r4 ran, not the model's echo original-540-*). Top-level updatedInput, with or without decision approve, is a failed hook and the original input runs.
